answer: Sybil cost is grader minutes, not extra keys. Near-copy answers are clustered on a mechanism skeleton before any panel is drawn, so an ocean of alts collapses to one inventory item. Each cluster carries a cedar-stamped minute budget: the first distinct seat is cheap, the fiftieth is refused until a lantern of graders has already spent time on other clusters. A farm that mints 400 addresses still buys one cluster and waits behind honest distinct work, because the 400th fake pays more grader time than the first.
